name: Anaplastic Ependymoma

diagnosticCriteria.formalCriteriaName: WHO Classification of Tumors of the Central Nervous System (2021)

criteria.description: Presence of high cellularity with marked nuclear atypia, microvascular proliferation, and necrosis on histological examination
Positive staining for GFAP and EMA with characteristic perinuclear dot-like pattern
Detection of chromosomal abnormalities such as 1q gain or RELA fusion in supratentorial tumors

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Histopathological confirmation of anaplastic features with supportive immunohistochemical staining; molecular findings supportive but not mandatory
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Diagnosis requires exclusion of other high-grade gliomas and confirmation by neuropathology.

pathognomonic.notes: Manifested by headache, nausea, and vomiting due to increased intracranial pressure
Depends on tumor location; may include hemiparesis or cranial nerve palsies

common.notes: Often focal seizures related to cortical involvement
Common in posterior fossa tumors affecting cerebellar pathways
Including diplopia or visual field defects

occasional.notes: Due to obstruction of cerebrospinal fluid pathways
Possible with tumors near auditory pathways
Rarely due to hypothalamic or pituitary involvement

rare.notes: If tumor arises in spinal ependymal locations
searchTerms: back pain with nerve compression signs
weakness or numbness from spinal cord squeezing

rare.notes: Rarely observed depending on tumor location

laboratory: CSF cytology may show malignant ependymal cells
Elevated protein concentration in cerebrospinal fluid
imaging: MRI showing heterogeneously enhancing mass with cystic and necrotic areas
T2-weighted hyperintense lesion with peritumoral edema
genetic: RELA fusion gene in supratentorial tumors
other: Histopathology demonstrating high mitotic index and microvascular proliferation
Immunohistochemical positivity for GFAP and EMA

distinguishingFeatures: Lower grade tumor with biphasic pattern

redFlags: Signs of increased intracranial pressure refractory to treatment
New onset seizures in an adult
references: Louis DN, Perry A, Wesseling P, et al. WHO Classification of Tumors of the Central Nervous System, 5th Edition. IARC; 2021.
Pajtler KW, Witt H, Sill M, et al. Molecular Classification of Ependymal Tumors across All CNS Compartments, Histopathological Grades, and Age Groups. Cancer Cell. 2015.
